Autism Alters Feedback Evaluation, Not Raw Perception
items.snippet: Do autistic brains perceive the world differently, or do they evaluate decisions along a unique path? An EEG study from the Hebrew University shows autistic adults match neurotypicals in sensory accuracy, but exhibit distinct neural processing of mistakes, difficulty, and past feedback.

items.title: How Human Brains Outgrew Ape Brains
items.snippet: Humans share 99% of our coding DNA with chimps, so why are our brains three times larger? Comparing human, chimpanzee, and gorilla brain organoids reveals that nearly 600 genetic switches are dialed up in humans, driving stem cell branching that creates more neurons.

items.title: Extra weight may be aging your brain faster than you think
items.snippet: A major 24-year study involving more than 8,200 adults suggests that excess body weight may accelerate brain aging, leading to faster declines in memory, concentration, and decision-making skills. The connection was particularly strong among people over 65, raising concerns about the long-term effects of obesity on brain health.

items.title: Scientists find surprisingly little evidence that medical cannabis helps you sleep
items.snippet: A major new review challenges the growing enthusiasm for medical cannabis as an insomnia treatment, finding little reliable evidence that it improves sleep quality, sleep duration, or daytime functioning. Researchers caution that this doesn't mean cannabis is ineffective, only that existing studies are too weak to establish whether it works.

items.title: Inside the quiet reinvention of corporate learning
items.snippet: Psychologist Pauline Boss coined the term “ambiguous loss” to describe a grief with no clear boundaries, like that experienced by families whose loved ones were missing in action and who could neither grieve nor move on. Since ChatGPT arrived in late 2022, I’ve seen a version of it every day in my work with people across companies. Nothing has been taken from us, and yet something has disappeared.

items.title: Even moderate drinking linked to cancer and early death, major study finds
items.snippet: A major new study challenges the idea that moderate drinking is safe, finding that even relatively small amounts of alcohol increase the risk of cancer, heart disease, and premature death. Researchers found no overall health benefits from drinking and warn that consuming more than one alcoholic beverage per day can significantly increase long-term health risks.
